analysis.title: Record Profits, Red Screens: Goldman Admits The AI Boom Has Become A Cost-Of-Capital Problem
key_insights: Samsung's preliminary Q3 operating profit was KRW 107.4T (about $80B), its first quarter above KRW 100T. TSMC Q3 revenue was a record NT$1.49T (US$46.7B), about 50% higher y/y and above the top of guidance. Asia sold off anyway: Nikkei about -1.4%, KOSPI lower, Taiwan weaker.

Privorotsky's thesis: AI capital demand is crowding out other borrowers. 'Strong earnings simply aren't enough to offset the pressure from rates, energy and capital supply.' Backdrop cited: oil above $103, US 10Y around 5.3%, Fed minutes pointing to another hike later this year.

Post-GFC abundant savings and low rates are ending. Large sovereign financing needs now compete with a technology boom with unprecedented capital demands. SpaceX is seeking $40B and Broadcom is reportedly exploring more than $50B of financing.

SpaceX (SPCX) is seeking $40B (about $10B bank loans, $30B IG bonds) to buy Nvidia chips. Broadcom (AVGO) is arranging more than $50B to finance OpenAI's custom chips, with Apollo and Blackstone among lenders in talks. This is on top of Broadcom's $60B financing for Anthropic's build-out. Each deal is larger than the $39B 10Y auction.

Bondholders are pushing back. SpaceX 5Y CDS hit a record of about 197bps and its 2056 bonds fell to about 84.7 cents from 98.83 at issue in June. GS CAS desk said macro credit opened weaker, with additional spread widening after the SPCX financing plans.

Privorotsky argues that borrowers who expect 20-30% compounding IRRs on scarce compute will borrow at high single-digit rates, which strains consumers, small businesses and governments built for cheap capital.

On real yields, Privorotsky says they refuse to fall because a large supply of high-quality private-sector paper competes with sovereign duration. US 10Y touched 5.36% and 30Y 5.73% (both 24-year highs) before the 10Y closed at 5.28%. That is the 100th percentile since 2004. IG all-in yield (iBoxIG) is 6.47%, 100th percentile since 2010. The 10Y real yield is 2.90%.

The 10Y auction went well: $39B reopening, 2.77x cover, 5.300% high yield (1.7bps stop-through, highest 10Y auction yield since November 2000), indirects 80.3%, dealers 2.5% (lowest in 10Y history). Privorotsky says the 30Y auction today is the next test, and long-end vol and the implied/realized premium remain elevated.

Goldman macro research is not unanimous. It argues wider European sovereign spreads tighten financial conditions and limit further yield rises, and sees a bias toward lower yields for Bunds and Treasuries, with the Fed and ECB delivering their last hike in December.
FOMC minutes showed all participants backed September's hike to 3.75-4% and most saw another as likely appropriate by year-end. Waller said further hikes will likely be needed.

European sovereign stress persists: the OAT rally reversed, with contagion to Italy and Greece. OAT/Bund widened as much as 17bps to 144bps and BTP/Bund 15bps to 120bps. Privorotsky calls it a fragile equilibrium.

Credit dashboard as of Tuesday: USD IG OAS 80bps (7th percentile since 2010, unchanged on the month). USD CCC OAS 998bps, up 123bps in a month and 219bps in three months, 100th percentile on a three-year lookback and 9bps from the 1,007bp three-year max. HY 305bps and CDX HY 338bps, each about 35-38bps wider on the month. HYG shares outstanding up 38.8M in a month, iBoxHY yield 8.24%.

Privorotsky frames two outcomes: AI becomes self-financing from organic cash flow (making next hyperscaler earnings particularly important), or capital is rationed elsewhere and weaker parts of the economy break, with CCC spreads possibly showing early signs.

Oil: a product tanker (Acers) was hit about 94km north of Qatar, deep inside the Gulf. Privorotsky is less convinced there is a credible off ramp, citing deadlocked talks, extraordinarily expensive freight, a divergence between physical crude and paper benchmarks, and the approaching midterms. Brent was back above $105 (+5%) on an Axios report the US could resume major combat in Iran before the midterms.

Equity breadth is weak: the GS US Cyclicals vs equal-weight S&P ratio closed at 0.6920, a one-year low and about 9% below its Feb 6 high of 0.7585. Russell has underperformed NDX in 17 of the last 20 sessions. AAII sentiment is back to neutral, so the extreme-negative-sentiment tailwind is gone.

LG Electronics earnings disappointed despite revenue growth on logistics and input costs, which Privorotsky reads as a negative read-through for the corporate picture outside AI. Samsung's print was slightly below Street, its fourth straight record quarter, and shares slipped about 1%.

Next tests: today's 30Y auction (1pm ET) and a Treasury buyback of up to $6B of longer-dated debt, TSMC full Q3 results on Oct 15, Samsung divisional breakdown on Oct 29, and next hyperscaler earnings. The author says that if the 30Y tails and CCC OAS breaks 1,007bps, this becomes a trend.

tension_points.bull_case: AI micro signals are green. Borrowers expecting 20-30% IRRs on compute can afford high single-digit rates, the 10Y auction went well, and IG spreads remain contained.
tension_points.bear_case: AI and sovereign supply push up the cost of capital, squeezing CCC credits (998bps), small caps, cyclicals and consumers.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A 30Y auction tail or CCC OAS breaking the 1,007bp three-year max would turn the thesis into a trend. Hyperscalers showing AI is self-financing from cash flow would weaken it.

tension_points.bull_case: GS macro research sees wider European spreads tightening financial conditions, a bias toward lower Bund and Treasury yields, and last hikes from the Fed and ECB in December.
tension_points.bear_case: Privorotsky and the author say real yields will not fall while AI private-sector paper competes with Treasuries, and the Fed is still debating further hikes.
tension_points.what_invalidates: If the Fed and ECB deliver their last hike in December, the GS macro team's view would be supported. More hikes or clean auctions failing to lower yields would favor the crowding-out view.
